sentences.text: The tail vertebrae of Xianshanosaurus were procoelous, meaning they had concave front faces and convex back faces that formed ball-and-socket joints, a trait typical of titanosaurs.
Unlike many titanosaurs, the back ribs of Xianshanosaurus lacked pneumatic openings and the haemal arches had closed canals.
Xianshanosaurus was described in 2009 by a team of paleontologists led by Lü Junchang.
Fossils of Xianshanosaurus were found in the Mangchuan Formation in the Ruyang Basin, specifically in Shijiagou village, Liudian town, Luoyang city, Henan province, China.
It is debated whether Xianshanosaurus is a titanosaur, and its closest relative may be Daxiatitan, though its evolutionary relationships remain controversial.
Phylogenetic analyses have often regarded Xianshanosaurus as an unstable taxon with uncertain placement.
In some analyses where Euhelopodidae was treated as a non-neosauropod group, researchers recovered Daxiatitan as the sister taxon to Xianshanosaurus.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Xianshanosaurus as Euhelopodidae.
Xianshanosaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately between 125 and 100 million years ago, from the Aptian to Albian stages in what is now Asia.
The time range for Xianshanosaurus is estimated from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Aptian to Albian stages.
